package.name: xai-grok
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# XAI GROK, fully declarative.
#
# The node is a REALTIME VOICE session, not a text agent — `wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime` — so what
# unblocked it was `transport: ws` and the audio lane, built for openai-realtime. Its protocol is
# identical to OpenAI's realtime format event for event, which is why shared/tools.yaml reads the same.
#
# TWO SOCKETS ARE INVOLVED and only one is here: the vendor socket is this manifest's `run`, while the
# platform's audio socket to the browser is api/audio.yaml. That second lane exists only because MCP
# cannot carry binary audio; everything else this node emits reaches the client over MCP streaming.

name: xai-grok
displayName: xAI Grok
description: Voice conversations, image generation and video generation with xAI's Grok
# 2.1.0: grok-voice-think-fast-2.0 (model picker + reasoning dial + gated transcription), plus the
# transcript-accumulation and Q/A-log fixes proven live on the sibling realtime voice node.
# 2.2.0: Grok Imagine joins the package — XAIGrokImage (imagine-image-2.0, synchronous) and
# XAIGrokVideo (imagine-video-1.5, an async job the poll capability waits on).
# 2.3.0: XAIGrokVideoExtend — chained shots via /v1/videos/extensions, because one 15-second
# generation compresses a construction-to-function arc too far (probed live 2026-08-15).
version: 2.3.0
category: ai
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1777865512/gravity/icons/X_logo.jpg

features:
  - Realtime voice conversation with Grok, with MCP tool calling
  - Image generation with Grok Imagine, typography-strong, hosted URLs back
  - Short video generation from a prompt or a still image, with sound
  - Video extension, continuing an existing clip shot by shot

allowedHosts:
  - api.x.ai

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [bearer]
  # ws carries the voice session; json carries the Imagine REST calls.
  transport: [ws, json]
  # The video node waits on a render job. Without `poll` it would settle on the job RECEIPT
  # and emit that as the answer, with nothing anywhere reporting a problem.
  poll: true

credentials.xaiCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: xaiCredential
displayName: xAI
description: Credentials for xAI Grok API
documentationUrl: https://console.x.ai

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your xAI API key
    placeholder: xai-

shared.tools.yaml:
# The xAI Grok REALTIME tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does not belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it does not
# belong copied into a node either. It belongs here, exactly as `openai/shared/tools.yaml` holds the
# Responses protocol — imported whole:
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#
# WHY THIS IS NOT `openai/shared/tools.yaml`. Same vendor, different API, and three real differences
# rather than cosmetic ones:
#
#   the call event   Responses says `response.output_item.done` and needs a `when` to tell a function
#                    call from any other completed item. Realtime has a dedicated
#                    `response.function_call_arguments.done`, so no `when` is needed.
#   no toolsInto     Responses puts the tool list in each REQUEST. A realtime session declares it
#                    ONCE in the handshake, so there is no request field to name; run.yaml reads
#                    `services.mcpService.tools` into session.update itself.
#   no continuity    Responses chains turns with previous_response_id. THE SOCKET IS THE CONTINUITY:
#                    the conversation never ended, so there is nothing to chain.
#
# Also absent, and deliberately: `maxTurns` and `stuckAfterRepeats`. Both count turns, and a turn is
# one model call. Nothing to count here. What bounds a runaway session is the executor's own idle and
# duration ceiling.

# How ONE tool is offered. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters }

# HOW THE LIST IS RE-OFFERED once it has grown mid-call. A socket sends its tools once at the
# handshake, so growth has to be announced on purpose — this message is that announcement.
#
# ONLY `tools` in the session block: session.update MERGES rather than replaces (verified live on
# OpenAI 2026-08-12; xAI documents the same session.update semantics), so instructions, voice and
# turn detection survive untouched. Re-sending the whole session would be a second copy of the
# handshake, free to drift. No `type: realtime` key — xAI's session object does not carry one.
offer: >-
  return { type: 'session.update', session: { tools: tools } }

# HOW THE INSTRUCTIONS ARE RE-SENT when a region skill comes into force or is cleared. The same
# shape and the same reason as `offer`, for the other thing the handshake sent once: a skill is
# decided by WHERE the conversation is standing, so it can change at any moment, and a socket
# that never mentions it again leaves the model working to a prompt that no longer describes
# where it is.
#
# ONLY `instructions`, for the merge reason above. The configured prompt is repeated alongside
# `skillsText` because a merge REPLACES the field it names: sending the skills alone would drop
# the node's role. No `type: realtime` key, matching `offer`.
reinstruct: >-
  return { type: 'session.update',
           session: { instructions: config.systemPrompt + skillsText } }

# How a call ARRIVES. `match` is what makes a stream tractable: events keep coming for the whole
# conversation, and this says which of them is a tool call rather than a transcript or audio.
call:
  match: response.function_call_arguments.done
  id: "return response.call_id"
  name: "return response.name"
  # A JSON STRING, which the executor parses. The trap the schema warns about: passed through
  # unparsed, the tool receives a string where it expected its parameters.
  arguments: "return response.arguments"

# How the result goes BACK. TWO messages, because OpenAI separates them: the output joins the
# conversation, then a response is asked for. Without the second the model holds the result silently.
result: >-
  return [
    { type: 'conversation.item.create',
      item: { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output } },
    { type: 'response.create' }
  ]

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# The vendor's `usage` block (cost_in_usd_ticks + token counts) rides on the same response
# and the executor's usage collector picks it up on its own — nothing here has to emit it.

- emit: images
  from: response
  value: >-
    return ((calls.generate || {}).data || []).map(d => ({
      url: d.url || ((d.file_output || {}).public_url || ''),
      mimeType: d.mime_type || 'image/png'
    }))

# `generatedAt` is epoch milliseconds: the sandbox exposes Date.now() and refuses `new`, so
# there is no way to format an ISO date inside an expression.
- emit: metadata
  from: response
  value: >-
    return {
      model: 'grok-imagine-image-2.0',
      imageCount: ((calls.generate || {}).data || []).length,
      generatedAt: Date.now()
    }
files.api/run.yaml:
# One synchronous call. THE MODEL IS FIXED: grok-imagine-image-2.0 is the only image id the
# vendor documents (docs.x.ai REST reference, 2026-08-15; shipped 2026-08-07), so there is no
# choice to surface and a free-text field would only invite a value the endpoint rejects.
# When xAI ships a second id, this becomes an enum in config.yaml exactly as the voice node's
# model did.

- name: generate
  method: POST
  url: https://api.x.ai/v1/images/generations
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.xaiCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
  transport: json
  # Image generation is slow, and a multi-image request more so.
  timeoutMs: 300000
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

  body:
    model: grok-imagine-image-2.0
    prompt: "{{ config.prompt }}"
    n: "return config.imageCount || 1"
    # `auto` is a real value the vendor takes, not an omission — it means "pick the frame
    # that suits the prompt", so it is sent rather than dropped.
    aspect_ratio: "return config.aspectRatio || 'auto'"
    resolution: "return config.resolution || '1k'"
    # URLs, not b64_json: bytes through the graph would be megabytes of base64 per image,
    # and every consumer of this node wants a link — a template to display, the video node
    # to animate.
    response_format: url

  error:
    # A refusal or empty result can come back as a 200 with no data entries, which would
    # otherwise emit an empty array and look like success.
    when: "return !((response.data || []).length)"
    message: >-
      return 'Grok returned no images.'
        + (response.error ? ' ' + JSON.stringify(response.error) : '')
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [prompt]
  properties:
    prompt:
      type: string
      title: Image Prompt
      description: Describe the image to generate. Shared blocks work here.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:ai":
        editable: true
    imageCount:
      type: number
      title: Images
      description: How many variations come back for the one prompt.
      default: 1
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 10
    aspectRatio:
      type: string
      title: Aspect Ratio
      description: >-
        The shape of the frame. Auto lets the model pick whatever suits the prompt.
      enum: ["auto", "1:1", "16:9", "9:16", "4:3", "3:4", "3:2", "2:3", "2:1", "1:2"]
      default: auto
    resolution:
      type: string
      title: Resolution
      description: 2k renders sharper and costs the same per image; 1k returns faster.
      enum: [1k, 2k]
      enumNames: ["1K (1024px)", "2K (2048px)"]
      default: 1k
"ui:order": [prompt, imageCount, aspectRatio, resolution]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes, referenceable in the prompt
    required: false

outputs:
  # URLs rather than bytes, by choice: `response_format: url` keeps megabytes of base64 out
  # of the graph, and a hosted URL is what every consumer here actually wants — a template
  # displays it, and the video node takes it as its starting frame.
  - name: images
    type: array
    description: >-
      One entry per image: url, mimeType. Index first when reading one, e.g. images.0.url
  - name: metadata
    type: object
    description: model, imageCount, generatedAt

credentials:
  - name: xaiCredential
    required: true
    displayName: xAI
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: XAIGrokImage
# One call, one reply: the images endpoint is synchronous.
kind: PromiseNode

name: Grok Image
category: Media & Design
color: "#000000"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1777865512/gravity/icons/X_logo.jpg

description: Generate images from a description with Grok Imagine

whenToUse: >-
  Create an image from a description: a picture, illustration, photo or graphic that does not
  exist yet. Strong at legible typography and text inside the image, and returns finished
  images as hosted URLs ready to display or hand to another step. Animating a still into
  motion, and editing a photo that already exists, are different jobs.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (who-can-run-it.md). Compulsory on every node, so that a node nobody
# thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable. Generation is non-deterministic: asking twice is meant to produce two
  # different images, and reusing the first would be a bug rather than a saving.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# Asserts the SHAPE, not the picture: a hosted https URL per image and a matching count.
# Runs against the real service — one image at 1k, the cheapest honest request.

testData:
  config:
    prompt: >-
      A minimalist poster of a lighthouse at dusk, bold geometric shapes, the word
      "NORTH" in clean sans-serif lettering at the bottom
    imageCount: 1
    aspectRatio: "2:3"
    resolution: 1k
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    images: >-
      return output.images.length === 1
        && output.images[0].url.startsWith('https://')
        && output.images[0].mimeType.startsWith('image/')
    metadata: >-
      return output.metadata.imageCount === output.images.length
        && output.metadata.generatedAt > 0
